source.title: When Vision Transformers Outperform ResNets without Pretraining or Strong Data Augmentations
source.authors: Xiangning Chen; Cho-Jui Hsieh; Boqing Gong

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares convolutional and convolution-free vision architectures and reports that SAM changes their relative ImageNet performance, qualifying claims about architecture and generalization. It also compares SGD and Adam on ViT-B/16.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet accuracy and loss-geometry results for its own models. It does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, large-batch effects, dropout alone, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The optimizer comparison tests V4 in an ImageNet vision Transformer setting and finds AdamW outperforming momentum SGD. The architecture comparisons do not test V3's fully connected versus convolutional comparison, and the geometry measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SAM smooths loss landscapes and improves ViT and MLP-Mixer accuracy and robustness, enabling tested ViTs to outperform comparable ResNets without pretraining or strong augmentations. They also report approximately twice the computation per update and diminishing gains with larger training datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares ResNet, ViT and MLP-Mixer architectures and introduces SAM, which explicitly optimizes for local loss smoothness; this is not a reproduction of the listed original studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and model capacity; SAM perturbation strength; optimizer (SGD versus Adam); training-set size; strong augmentation and contrastive-learning settings. The paper reports these settings affect performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Without SAM, ResNet-152 reaches 78.5% ImageNet accuracy, versus 74.6% for ViT-B/16 and 66.4% for Mixer-B/16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the reported basic preprocessing and architecture-specific recipes, ResNet-152 outperforms these vision Transformer and MLP-Mixer models.

fits_no_version.finding: With SAM, ViT-B/16 exceeds ResNet-152 at 79.9% versus 79.3%, and ViT-S/16 exceeds ResNet-50 at 78.1% versus 76.7%; Mixer-B/16 remains below ResNet-152 at 77.4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture rankings among ResNets, vision Transformers, and MLP-Mixers depend on the training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM lowers Gaussian-perturbed training loss from 2.39 to 2.16 for ResNet-152, 6.66 to 0.96 for ViT-B/16, and 7.78 to 1.01 for Mixer-B/16, alongside higher validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM improves the tested models' validation accuracy while reducing average training loss under Gaussian weight perturbations.

record.problems: The architecture comparison is not against fully connected networks and does not isolate local connectivity. The paper reports point accuracies without uncertainty estimates. Its loss-geometry measurements are not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7 and do not by themselves establish a generalization-gap ranking.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable result rows omitted. Several reported accuracy comparisons on ImageNet-ReaL, ImageNet V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-C, adversarial training, contrastive learning, and transfer tasks are outside the natural-label in-distribution accuracy comparisons captured here.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under random versus natural labels.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold; the model-size comparisons do not locate that threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, the contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, and convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.

A controlled learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning comparison is not established. Training-performance comparisons between SGD and AdamW, other adaptive optimizers, language benchmarks, broader matched tuning, isolated decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers are untested.
Batch-size effects at a fixed epoch budget. Subset experiments change both training data and batch size; throughput sweeps do not measure generalization.
Isolated dropout effects, dependence on training-set size, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps within a convolutional family, including comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. V4's 'often' wording permits exceptions: these results establish an opposite-direction case, not a general refutation. Architecture comparisons also use different optimizers, regularization, and epoch budgets across families.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.

The comparison is ResNets versus ViTs and MLP-Mixers, not fully connected networks; local connectivity is not isolated, and the paper does not test convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Other adaptive optimizers, language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay as an isolated intervention, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's isolated effect across training-set sizes and its interaction with weight decay removal.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining on memorized examples versus random-example removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-152
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla training with basic Inception-style preprocessing; compared with SAM-trained counterpart.
rows.note: Reference convolutional architecture in the reported comparison.
rows.check: Accuracy 78.5% is correct, but the comparators are ViTs and structured MLP-Mixers rather than the fully connected networks named in V3. Table 12 specifies momentum SGD and 90 epochs.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla training with basic Inception-style preprocessing; compared with SAM-trained counterpart.
rows.note: Lower than the reported ResNet-152 result.
rows.check: Accuracy 74.6% is correct. A vision Transformer is outside V3's fully connected comparator; its lower accuracy cannot establish that version.

rows.subject: Mixer-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla training with basic Inception-style preprocessing; compared with SAM-trained counterpart.
rows.note: Lower than the reported ResNet-152 result.
rows.check: Accuracy 66.4% is correct. Mixer uses patch embeddings and structured token/channel MLPs; a convolution-free architecture is not automatically the fully connected network named in V3.

rows.subject: ResNet-152-SAM
rows.operation_detail: SAM training with basic Inception-style preprocessing.
rows.note: The table reports +0.8 over the vanilla counterpart.
rows.check: The 78.5% to 79.3% improvement measures SAM's performance, not a listed claim. SAM is applied over momentum SGD.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16-SAM
rows.operation_detail: SAM training with basic Inception-style preprocessing.
rows.note: The table reports +5.3 over vanilla; the result exceeds ResNet-152-SAM.
rows.check: The 74.6% to 79.9% improvement is correct but measures SAM's performance. Exceeding a ResNet with a Transformer does not reverse V3's fully connected comparison.

rows.subject: Mixer-B/16-SAM
rows.operation_detail: SAM training with basic Inception-style preprocessing.
rows.note: The table reports +11.0 over vanilla; this result remains below ResNet-152-SAM.
rows.check: The 66.4% to 77.4% improvement is correct but measures SAM's performance. Even under the reader's broader architecture interpretation, 77.4% remains below ResNet-152-SAM's 79.3%, so 'reversed' was incorrect.

rows.subject: ResNet-50-SAM
rows.operation_detail: SAM training with basic Inception-style preprocessing.
rows.note: Reference for the similar-size ViT-S/16 comparison.
rows.check: Accuracy 76.7% is correct, but comparison with a vision Transformer does not test V3.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16-SAM
rows.operation_detail: SAM training with basic Inception-style preprocessing.
rows.note: The paper states this is 1.4 percentage points above similarly sized ResNet-50-SAM.
rows.check: Accuracy 78.1% is correct, but the subject is a vision Transformer rather than V3's fully connected network.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.locator: Section 4.2, “SAM can be easily applied to common base optimizers”
rows.note: Text directly compares SGD-only with Adam at the same stated 300-epoch budget.
rows.check: The direction was inverted: momentum SGD reaches 71.5%, below the adaptive optimizer's 74.6%. The prose calls the adaptive optimizer Adam, while Table 12 specifies AdamW. The SGD-specific tuning procedure is not fully reported.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.locator: Section 4.2, “SAM can be easily applied to common base optimizers”
rows.note: The paper reports +7.6 absolute improvement over SGD-only; Adam + SAM reaches 79.9%.
rows.check: For V4, compare momentum SGD + SAM at 79.1% with AdamW + SAM at 79.9% in R11. The increase over SGD alone measures SAM's effect and cannot establish the adaptive-versus-SGD direction.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.locator: Section 4.2, “SAM can be easily applied to common base optimizers”; Table 1
rows.note: The text says the Adam + SAM and SGD + SAM gap largely shrinks.
rows.check: AdamW + SAM reaches 79.9%, exceeding momentum SGD + SAM's 79.1%; this reverses the adaptive-disadvantage direction. Its 74.6% baseline measures improvement from SAM, not the optimizer comparison.
